clue.text: Where a Frenchman embraces his lady-love?

definitions.text: Where a Frenchman embraces his lady-love?

parts.words: Where a Frenchman embraces his lady-love?
parts.note: suggests a romantic spot, but points to the small second home in town kept, in the comic tradition, for meeting a mistress

explanation.surface: A question about where a French lover meets his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase literally means 'foot on the ground'; the clue plays on the cliché of a discreet city flat used for affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secondary lodging, the stereotypical setting for a French gentleman's discreet liaisons.

clue.text: Fear of a deity perhaps

explanation.surface: A dread of some god.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden terror; as an adjective with a capital it means relating to Pan, the Greek god of the wild.

clue.text: Found attempt to interrupt prophet cut short

indicators.note: to interrupt puts one piece in the middle of the other
cut short means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: Elisha was an Old Testament prophet
a stab is an attempt

explanation.surface: A prophet's attempt to speak is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find but is the verb meaning set up; 'cut short' drops the prophet's last letter and 'to interrupt' puts the attempt inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up.

clue.text: No fee, people say, can make up for something cherished

indicators.note: make up here means form something new from the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: People claiming nothing can compensate for losing a treasured thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make up' rearranges the letters of 'No fee, people say'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person or thing held most dear.

clue.text: Bears close to river start to snuffle

parts.note: close means the end
the Ure is a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Bears near a river begin sniffing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like animals but is the verb; the Ure is a crosswords' favourite river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it, tolerate it.

clue.text: Soldiers not finishing course

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops failing to complete an assault course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts T from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed programme of diet or exercise is a course of treatment.

clue.text: Dwelling of note

explanation.surface: Describing a home of some distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a home on one floor; in music a note lowered a semitone is marked that way.

clue.text: One included in older type of transport

indicators.note: included in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: LNER, the London and North Eastern Railway, was an old British railway company
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone travelling in an old-fashioned vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts I inside LNER, a pre-1948 British railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean passenger ship is a means of transport.

clue.text: Finally got involved, and -was a representative

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: ravelled means tangled, involved

explanation.surface: A salesman who eventually got caught up in things.
explanation.walkthrough: A representative (sales rep) travels for a living, so the past tense fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a salesman, so to have toured selling goods is to have worked as one.

clue.text: Entire channels reallocated, intended for light broadcasting

indicators.note: reallocated means the letters are redistributed in another order

explanation.surface: Broadcast channels reorganised for light entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reallocated' rearranges 'Entire channels'; 'intended for' and 'broadcasting' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper lamp with a candle inside gives light.

clue.text: Press Association going into well-known group of papers

indicators.note: going into tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: well-known means noted, famous
PA is the standard abbreviation for the Press Association news agency

explanation.surface: A news agency joining a famous newspaper group.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'group of papers' sounds like a newspaper group, but it is a stationery item; 'going into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is a block of sheets stuck together for jotting on.

clue.text: Hell, say, turned red

indicators.note: turned tells us the short word for 'say' is read backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
henna is a reddish dye, so red stands for it

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that hell has gone red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses only the abbreviation for 'say'. The comma after 'Hell' hides that 'say' is a separate piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical valley of fire became a name for the place of damnation.

clue.text: Chap belted girl — aims oddly to convey a message

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the run of words before it

explanation.surface: A man who has struck a girl tries strangely to send a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Counting through 'Chap belted girl aims' as one run, the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on give the answer; 'to convey a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by undersea wire is a kind of message.

clue.text: Language used by sixteen or seventeen-year-olds

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Teenage slang spoken by sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'sixteeN OR SEventeen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings is a language.

clue.text: Put in the picture, in short

explanation.surface: Telling someone the facts concisely.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in the picture is to inform them before a task; short and concise mean the same.

clue.text: Bankrupt, despite making no loss (or profit)

parts.note: to break someone is to ruin them financially
even, as in 'even so', carries the sense of despite

explanation.surface: Ruined, although the business made neither loss nor gain.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis completes the definition: neither loss nor profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out level, with income equal to costs.

clue.text: Spill the beans at entrance to shopping arcade and become crestfallen

parts.note: to spill the beans is to confess, slang sing

indicators.note: entrance to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a shopping arcade is a mall

explanation.surface: Someone blabbing a secret at the door of a shopping centre, then feeling ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing small is an idiom for being humbled, adopting a meek tone.

clue.text: Set pop up with a tip

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: pop means father, pa
having a tip means pointed

explanation.surface: Setting a pop record up with a pointer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PA into AP.
explanation.definitionFit: A set time is one fixed or arranged in advance.

clue.text: People risking losing their heads — it's increasing

indicators.note: losing their heads means each of the two words drops its first letter

parts.note: people means men, and risking means chancing

explanation.surface: Daredevils in danger of decapitation, a risk that grows.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN loses M and CHANCING loses C; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or improve something is to make it greater, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Executed prime minister of a foreign state

indicators.note: executed suggests beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A foreign premier who was put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' means beheaded: Disraeli loses his D. The surface suggests the definition is the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the Middle Eastern nation founded in 1948.

clue.text: Sharing out the decoration

indicators.note: out here suggests the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Dividing up the decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges 'Sharing'; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimming added to a dish to improve its look.

clue.text: Was first out of work and ran

indicators.note: out of here means the outer piece sits outside the other

parts.note: was first means led, as in led the race
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone who was the first to lose their job, then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' here means outside: the leader's word goes round the work, not out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long bounding strides.

clue.text: Lined up, we hear, to get great honour

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the words before it

parts.note: lined up means queued, which said aloud with a following 'oss' sound gives the answer

explanation.surface: People waiting in line to receive an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: 'queued' gives the first part of the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige or acclaim earned for an achievement.

clue.text: Material dug up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: dug means mined

explanation.surface: Fabric excavated from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MINED round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardwearing cotton twill is a fabric.

clue.text: Giving second showing of film about sovereign without a break

indicators.note: about tells us the letters for the monarch are turned round

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
without a break means continuously, running

explanation.surface: A documentary about a monarch shown non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes RE from ER; 'about' looks like it means 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Screening again is repeating a showing, broadcasting it a second time.

clue.text: Unexpected money is put into a boat

explanation.surface: A windfall stowed in a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus windfall is slang for easy money; the meat sauce is served from a jug shaped like a boat.

clue.text: Artist who depicted a wagon beside the water

parts.note: a van is a covered wagon
a dyke can be a watercourse or ditch

explanation.surface: A painter who painted a cart by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who depicted a' and 'beside' are links; the clue nods to Constable-style rustic scenes. The Flemish portraitist is usually spelt Van Dyck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish painter famed for royal portraits was a Baroque artist.

clue.text: In it are characters displaying sloth

indicators.note: characters here means the letters of the words before it, rearranged

explanation.surface: Some figures in a story show laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like story people but means the letters of 'In it are'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy or idleness, a lack of will to move.

clue.text: Call Englishman back

indicators.note: back says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: E for English plus man

explanation.surface: Telling an English man to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EMAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to give them a title or label.

clue.text: Stranded dinghy hard to refloat

indicators.note: to refloat suggests the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A small boat beached that is difficult to get back on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to refloat' rearranges 'dinghy hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Left without help, like a boat beached by the tide.
